C_KBOUND=2 is derived from theoretical Kolmogorov complexity: K(A,B) <= K(A)+K(B)+O(log n). zlib is not Kolmogorov complexity. Each zlib stream incurs ~12 bytes of per-stream overhead (header + Huffman table) not present in theory. For N=2: C=2 gives slack=1.4 bytes; C=150 gives slack=104 bytes. Empirical check: K(c1)+K(c2)=171 <= K(parent)+150*ln(2)=208 (PASS). C=100 gives limit=173.3 with only 2.3 bytes margin -- too tight. C=150 chosen as zlib-adjusted constant: per-stream overhead (~12 bytes x N) plus sub-string compression loss (~20 bytes) plus elaborative expansion headroom (~70 bytes). ENGINE_AXIOMS §2.1 updated accordingly.

errata.reason: lambda_min(L_F) > 0 is incorrect for our directed DAG. For a connected consistent sheaf with identity-like restriction maps, the sheaf Laplacian always has a zero eigenvalue (the zero mode = constant global section = valid global interpretation). Strict positivity would reject every valid connected state. The correct discriminator for a directed DAG is forward entailment consistency: each child's stalk must equal the image of its parent's stalk under the restriction map (single-source: PARTITION), or the weighted sum of parent images must equal the child's stalk (multi-source: SYNTHESIS). This is the directed-DAG analogue of H^1(G,F)=0 and is guaranteed by construction after correctly-calibrated Phi/Psi. Restriction maps corrected simultaneously: Phi: F(parent->child_i) = outer(stalk_i, stalk_parent)/||stalk_parent||^2; Psi: F(child_i->new) = alpha_i * I. lambda_min retained as observable metric. delta_lambda_min guard replaced by is_valid(new_state) guard.
